review_type: fresh independent final whole-bank raw-source coverage challenge

files.note: Manifest itself has no externally supplied expected digest; recorded for reproducibility.

scope_and_authority.governing_scope: Original Nemesis basic-board standard semi-cooperative core, six original characters. Original English 28-page manual (including illustrations), official FAQ v2.2 base-game Rules/Actions/Rooms/Items, compatible supplemental wording in original publisher-hosted localizations. Optional modes, boards, campaigns and expansions excluded.

faq_scope.included: Rules1–26 except17–18; Actions1–19 except16; Rooms1–9; Items1–10
faq_scope.excluded: Cooperative Rules17–18, Intruder-player Actions16 and expansion FAQ sections

scope_and_authority.localizations: Listed PL/FR/DE original publisher-hosted manuals corroborate compatible English wording only. They are neither universal English errata nor independent authority for arbitrary additional outcomes. Examples include PL/FR miss-conditioned Egg waiver and Slime-entry order, and compatible illustrated card icons/effects.
scope_and_authority.author_map: Read as challengeable author claims. Its additions, topic labels, novelty descriptions and zero-addition passes were not treated as proof. All support and closure decisions below are from current requests/keys and permitted primary evidence.

required_parts.required: Use the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, paying 2 Action cards in that Room; the Pod must be Unlocked with a free Character space, and an Intruder or Malfunction in the Section prevents entry. Being outside Combat is the same Intruder restriction here.
First resolve the Noise roll. An Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes the attempt fail.
Two Character spaces per Pod; Heavy Objects consume no Character space. This is not a separate unlimited-Hand-capacity rule.
Choosing to wait after boarding passes the current turn and leaves the Character treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls.
At the start of the Character’s first round in each later Player Phase, choose to remain waiting and pass, launch, or exit free to the corresponding Section Room and play a full two-Action round.
A new boarder may immediately launch with both occupants, even if the first occupant chose to wait.
An Intruder appearing in the Section immediately returns every Character in any Pod of that Section to the Section Room.
A Malfunction appearing in the Section does not remove the already-boarded Character’s choices to wait, launch, or exit; it blocks only new entry.

context_not_automatically_required.fact: Immediate launch instead of initially waiting
context_not_automatically_required.reason: The stem asks about waiting options and consequences, rather than expressly asking for every initial post-boarding alternative. This correct extra fact can help frame the answer but its absence alone is not the basis for a partial grade.

context_not_automatically_required.fact: Launching removes Pod and miniatures, ends active participation, and counts as arriving on Earth while preserving final Contamination and Objective checks
context_not_automatically_required.reason: The waiting branch must identify launch as an option. The stem does not independently request the entire endgame procedure or a survival/win ruling. If a response supplies these details, they must nevertheless be factually assessed.

context_not_automatically_required.fact: How Pods become Unlocked, initial Locked state, and automatic unlocking triggers
context_not_automatically_required.reason: Identifying an Unlocked Pod as an entry condition resolves the stem without explaining all ways to create that condition.

scope_and_authority.novelty_standard: Distinct material source-backed procedure, outcome, exception or information boundary beyond closest actual requests/keyed clauses. Names, costs, quantities and mechanical recombinations alone fail. Correct volunteered key context does not become an actually requested branch.
scope_and_authority.excluded: Alternative board, optional modes, solo/cooperative changes, Intruder-player mode, campaigns, expansions, external rulings, unseen physical-card text and unresolved hypothetical-state outcomes.

inspection_record.question_and_key_read: All127 actual question strings and complete expected answers read and checked. Supporting key metadata/ref lists were read as traceability, not primary proof.
inspection_record.english_manual: Complete extracted English manual read; all28 original PDF pages visually swept. Native readable illustrations inspected at larger size, particularly pp3,10,13,18–23,25–26. Page3 native image assets enlarged to distinguish readable samples from uncertain/cropped clauses.
inspection_record.faq: All61 scoped entries read in extraction and visually verified on raw PDF pp2–4.
inspection_record.localizations: All six listed PL/FR/DE PDF/text input hashes verified. Relevant original texts and illustrated corroboration inspected: PL/FR pp13,19,23,25; DE pp19,22,23,25. No claim of complete localization-card corpus or complete visual legibility.

question_review.actual_question: In a four-player standard game, how many Escape Pods are selected, how are they distributed and oriented, and which tokens start in the Intruder bag?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Three random pods; lowest numbered in A, next B, next A, all Locked. Bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 7 Adults.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Four-player setup asks the pod-selection/distribution/Locked state and complete bag recipe; all are explicit in setup steps7,10.

question_review.actual_question: How are Objectives filtered and dealt, when does each player choose one, what happens to the rejected card, and do Eggs trigger that choice?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Remove Objectives requiring more players than present; deal one Personal and one Corporate secretly. First Intruder miniature of any type appearing triggers immediate choice by everyone before resolving its Encounter. Remove rejected card face down unseen. Eggs do not trigger it.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests filtering, secret Personal/Corporate dealing, first miniature timing, rejected-card secrecy and Eggs exclusion; all explicitly supported.

question_review.actual_question: You use an Action card with printed cost 2 while holding that card, two other Action cards and two Contamination cards. What is discarded, and can Contamination substitute for payment? What if the card offers OR effects?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Discard the played card and two additional Action cards face up. Contamination cannot pay costs. Choose one OR effect.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests played-card versus additional payment, Contamination ineligibility and OR choice. Printed cost is additional to the played card.

question_review.actual_question: A Character in a burning Room takes one Action then passes. When do they take Fire damage, can they act again this Player Phase, can they discard cards, and do later players rounds burn them again?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: At end of own round take 1 Light Wound. Passing bars normal Actions this Player Phase, but official FAQ permits Interruption after passing. May discard any number of hand cards on passing. No further Fire wounds from later players rounds this turn.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests one-Action/pass Fire timing, later-action restriction, discretionary hand discards and no repeated Fire from others rounds. Interruption is the FAQ exception.

question_review.actual_question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests the exploration sequence, Item Counter exceptions, exploration effect/removal and occupied-Room or Silence/Danger alteration of Noise. Does not request every board-wide Noise property; Q111 supplies that.

question_review.actual_question: What does Careful Movement cost and replace, when is it forbidden, and can a Closed Door be crossed or a miniature stop in a Corridor?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Cost 2 Action cards; replaces post-movement Noise roll with placing Noise in a chosen connected Corridor. Forbidden in Combat or when all destination Corridors have Noise. Closed Doors block player movement; no miniature stops in Corridors.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Careful Movement payment/replacement/forbidden states, Closed Door movement and no stopping in Corridors. FAQ Q86 separately handles automatic exploration Noise.

question_review.actual_question: You roll a number for a Corridor already holding Noise, with a Technical Corridors Entrance in your Room. Give the Encounter sequence, Noise removal, token destination and Surprise Attack comparison; do Contamination cards count?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Resolve Encounter: remove all connected Noise including Technical Corridors; draw bag token; place matching Intruder; compare token number to all cards in triggering hand including Contamination. Fewer cards causes Surprise Attack against triggerer, equal or more does not. Set token aside.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Encounter ordering, connected/Technical Noise removal, token set-aside and triggering-hand comparison including Contamination. Not ordinary-attack fewest-Action-card targeting.

question_review.actual_question: How does Danger resolve with several eligible neighboring Intruders, and when none are eligible? Does moving an Intruder into your Room count as an Encounter? How does Slime affect Silence?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Move all neighboring Intruders not in Combat into current Room. If none eligible, put Noise in each connected Corridor lacking it including Technical Corridors. Moving Intruder into occupied Room is Combat, not Encounter. Slime converts Silence Noise/exploration results to Danger.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests all eligible neighboring Intruders, no-eligible placement only into Corridors without Noise, movement-versus-Encounter distinction and Slimed Silence conversion.

question_review.actual_question: During an Encounter you draw Blank. What happens to Noise and the Blank; when is an Adult added? Contrast Blank in bag development.
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Encounter replaces connected Noise in every Corridor; return Blank; add Adult only if Blank was last token in bag and a spare Adult is available; no miniature or Surprise Attack. Development always attempts adding one available Adult then returns Blank.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Blank Encounter Noise replacement, token return and conditional last-token Adult addition, contrasted with development. No invented miniature/Surprise on Blank.

question_review.actual_question: Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Both stay in original Room and destroy Door simultaneously. Destroyed Door permits movement but cannot close except Plasma Torch. Noise-triggered appearance ignores Closed Door.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests simultaneous blocked Intruder movement, destruction/permanence/Plasma Torch exception and a Noise appearance despite the Door.

question_review.actual_question: An injured Intruder moves into Technical Corridors with Noise already there. What happens to its miniature, injuries, token and Noise? Can Characters or Doors normally use those Corridors?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Remove miniature, discard injuries, return matching token to bag; keep Noise. Characters barred except Mechanic Technical Corridors card and Technical Corridor Plans Item; Doors never placed there.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests ducts removing miniature/injuries but preserving Noise and returning matching token, plus ordinary Character/Door prohibition and named card exceptions.

question_review.actual_question: Describe an ordinary Shoot versus Melee Action: card/ammo costs, target location, Contamination, a miss, and the two-hit die result.
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Both cost 1 Action card against target in same Room. Shoot needs Weapon in Hand and spends 1 Ammo; normal two-hit deals 2 injuries subject to Weapon. Melee draws Contamination to Action discard before choosing target, miss causes Serious Wound, two-hit deals only 1 injury.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests ordinary Shoot/Melee payment, Ammo/Hand/location, pre-target Contamination, miss and two-hit distinction. It does not request all special Weapons; Q115/Q120/Q123 test specific overrides.

question_review.actual_question: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Larva dies at 1 injury without Carcass. Adult draws one Attack card blood, dies if blood <= current injuries and leaves Carcass. Queen draws two, sums blood and compares same way; any Retreat arrow causes retreat via Event-card corridor number, discard Event, rather than normal numerical resolution. Any killed non-Larva Intruder, including Queen, leaves a Carcass in its death Room; Larva does not.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Larva/Adult/Queen death checks, Carcass and Queen Retreat-arrow priority. p22 general Carcass clause confirms Queen as well as Adult. No numeric hit-point constancy is implied.

author_key_source_references_for_traceab.location: Heavy Objects: Carcass after death of any Intruder except Larvae

question_review.actual_question: A Character Escapes a Room with two Intruders toward an empty unexplored Room. When do attacks occur, who is targeted, what happens if they die, and what follows if they survive?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Pay Movement cost 1, choose neighboring Room. Before moving resolve separate Attack from each Intruder targeting escaper. Death leaves Corpse in starting Room; survival completes move and standard exploration/Noise.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests each pre-move Escape Attack, escaper targeting, death in starting Room and ordinary exploration/Noise after survival.

question_review.actual_question: In an ordinary Intruder Attack with several Characters, how is the target chosen and ties broken; how is a hit determined; what changes for Larva and where does its Contamination go?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Fewest Action cards in hand; tie First Player or next in turn order. Matching attacker symbol on drawn Attack card means resolve effect; otherwise miss; ignore blood and discard card. Larva draws no Attack card: place miniature on target Character board and give Contamination on top of Action discard.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests fewest Action cards (rather than all cards), tie order, matching attack symbol/ignore blood, Larva infest procedure and Contamination discard destination.

question_review.actual_question: At three Serious Wounds, does dressing one prevent death from a Light Wound? What happens at a third Light Wound otherwise, what does Heal remove, and where do a dead Characters Corpse and Heavy Objects go?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: No: dressed still counts; any further Wound kills at three Serious. Third Light clears Light track and causes Serious Wound. Heal removes specified Light Wound or discards dressed Serious card. Place Corpse and drop Heavy Objects in death Room.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests dressed Serious count/death threshold, third-Light conversion, Heal meaning, Corpse and Heavy Objects at death. Dress suppresses effects without reducing count.

question_review.actual_question: Contrast Canteen/Shower scanning with Surgery: which cards are scanned and removed, how is a Larva handled, and what costs or turn consequences follow Surgery?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Canteen/Shower optionally scan hand Contamination, remove non-Infected; infected gives Larva and retains card, existing Larva means death/Creeper. Canteen heals 1 Light; Shower removes Slime. Surgery scans deck/hand/discard, removes infected and Larva, then 1 Light Wound, automatic pass, shuffle all cards including hand into deck; empty hand until next turn.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests scan scope/removal/Larva and Surgery wound/pass/shuffle/empty-hand consequences. Non-scanning benefits in its key are correct context; Q126 actually requests their coupling to optional scanning.

question_review.actual_question: How can uncarried Eggs be destroyed with Shoot/Melee, grenades, Molotov and Fire; which Melee penalties are waived, when is Noise rolled and when is the Nest destroyed?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Each Injury from Shoot/Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. Successful Egg Melee retains the ordinary draw of 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. On a missed Egg Melee, no Contamination card and no Wound are suffered. The sources do not specify how the normal pre-roll draw and miss waiver are reconciled; no refund or delayed draw is invented. Grenade destroys 2 Eggs, Molotov 1; Noise after every destruction attempt including miss. Fire destroys 1 uncarried Egg each Fire Damage step. Nest destroyed once all its Eggs taken/destroyed; mark Injury in Nest.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Egg destruction methods, miss waiver, mandatory attempt Noise and Nest destruction. English ordinary Melee draws before rolling; English/PL/FR Egg exception is miss-conditioned. Successful draw is retained; no refund or delayed-draw algorithm is asserted. Execution timing on miss remains unresolved.

question_review.actual_question: What permits or prevents entering an Escape Pod, what must you resolve first, how many Characters and Heavy Objects fit, and what are the options and consequences when you wait?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Use the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action in that Room, paying 2 Action cards. The Pod must be Unlocked with a free Character space; an Intruder or Malfunction in the Section prevents entry. Resolve Noise first; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes boarding fail. Each Pod has two Character spaces; Heavy Objects use none. After boarding one may launch immediately or choose to wait. Waiting passes the current turn and the Character is treated as present in the Section for bag-development Noise rolls. At the start of the Character’s first round in each later Player Phase choose wait/pass, launch, or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full two-Action round. If an Intruder appears in the Section, immediately return every Character in any Pod of that Section to its Room. A new boarder may immediately launch both occupants. A later Malfunction does not remove an already-boarded Character’s normal wait/launch/exit choices; it only blocks new entry.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Fixed accepted literal scope applied in full: entry/payment/restrictions, prior Noise/failure, spaces/Heavy Objects, initial wait/pass/Noise exposure, later timed choices, second boarder, Intruder return and later-Malfunction distinction. Immediate launch and complete launch/endgame procedure remain correct context rather than newly required Q19 parts.

question_review.actual_question: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Engines then Coordinates then Contamination then Objectives. If ship survives to checks: two/three Damaged explodes kills all aboard incl Intruders; non-Earth kills sleepers but ship/Intruders survive, Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. All survivors including launched pod passengers scan all Contamination; any infected triggers shuffle all Action/Contamination draw 4, any Contamination kills else survives. Larva skips scanning and directly does shuffle/draw. Survivors then reveal/check chosen Objective.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests ordered Engines/Coordinates/Contamination/Objectives checks and stated survival branches including Quarantine and pod passengers. Larva goes directly to shuffle/draw.

question_review.actual_question: How are the basic and additional Room tiles and Exploration tokens placed at setup; what Coordinates, Destination, Time, Engines, Eggs and Weaknesses start on the board?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: All 11 basic tiles face down in 1 slots; five random additional tiles face down in 2 slots, leftovers boxed unseen; random face-down Exploration per tile. Random face-down Coordinates, Destination B, Time green. Each numbered Engine has shuffled Damaged/Working pair face down, top true status. Five Eggs, three random face-down Weaknesses.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Room/Exploration setup and listed board tracks/cards/tokens. Engine top token is secret true state; basic Rooms all used and only five additional selected.

question_review.actual_question: How are Player Numbers assigned and Characters drafted; what does each Character receive and where do Characters and the initial Corpse begin? Are Quest Items usable immediately?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Random Help cards 1 through player count with matching Inventories assign Player Numbers; in number order draw two draft cards, reveal, choose one, shuffle other back. Receive board, ringed miniature in Hibernatorium, shuffled 10 Action cards, starting Weapon in Hand fully loaded, two horizontal inactive Quest Items; activate by printed quest then ordinary Items. Player 1 First Player; blue Corpse in Hibernatorium is Character Corpse Object.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests player numbering, revealed two-choice draft, per-Character components/starting position, initial blue Corpse and inactive Quest Items. Original six Characters only.

question_review.actual_question: When are Action hands refilled and the First Player token passed; what happens when the Action deck empties, and what are the normal discard destinations and visibility?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: At Player Phase start draw to 5, shuffle Action discard whenever required draw finds empty deck; then pass token left except first turn. Actions/Contamination to own Action discard, Items/Event/Attack/Serious Wounds to respective discard piles face up; markers to pools. Search example has explicit face-down return exception.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests refill/token timing, draw-driven empty-deck reshuffle and discard destinations/visibility. Rejected Search-card return is the face-down exception, with bottom placement fixed by FAQ.

question_review.actual_question: Give the Event Phase order, which Intruders move on an Event card, what controls movement and when the event effect resolves; what happens when Event and Intruder Attack decks run out?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Time and active Self-Destruct advance, Intruders in Combat attack, Fire Damage, Event card movement then effect, bag development fully resolved before next turn. Move symbol-matching Intruders without Characters in Room via card-number Corridor; ducts remove miniature/return token. Discard Event unless instructed otherwise. Empty Event/Attack decks reshuffle their respective discard piles.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests all Event steps, symbol/number-controlled non-Combat movement, movement before effect and exhaustion reshuffles. Does not itself request Coolant Leak immediate non-exhaustion reshuffle; Q129 does.

question_review.actual_question: In bag development, describe Larva, Creeper, Adult, Breeder and both Queen branches. Which tokens are removed or returned, who rolls Noise and when does the next turn begin?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Larva removed to token pool, add Adult; Creeper removed to pool, add Breeder. Adult/Breeder cause ordered Noise rolls excluding Combat; token returns. For Adult specifically, return token immediately BEFORE Noise so same token may be redrawn in an Encounter. Queen: Characters in Nest means Queen there and Encounter; otherwise including undiscovered Nest add Egg; return Queen. Fully resolve triggered effects before new turn.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests all listed bag branches and token/Noise/end-turn timing. Adult is returned before Noise by FAQ; generic Breeder order is not silently promoted to an additional erratum.

question_review.actual_question: When do Fire and Malfunction exhaustion end the game; what if the target Room already has that marker, and where do removed markers go? What happens to sleepers and Intruders when hull integrity is lost?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Eight of each; required new placement with no pool marker explodes/loses hull integrity, all aboard including sleepers/Intruders die. Existing same marker means nothing happens; max one per Room. Removed markers return to pools.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests new ninth Fire/Malfunction exhaustion, same-marker no-op, pool return and ship/sleeper/Intruder consequences.

question_review.actual_question: What does a Malfunction disable and leave usable, where can it never be placed, and does it change an Engine token or harm an already-hibernating Character?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Disables Room Action and Computer; Search still works. Never in Nest or Room Covered In Slime. Special Rooms can malfunction; Engine Working/Damaged unaffected and already-hibernating Characters unaffected. Repair cards/Tools can remove marker.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Room Action/Computer disability while Search survives, placement exclusions and lack of change to Engine state/sleepers.

question_review.actual_question: Which Items may be hidden, what do other players see, what is the Inventory limit, and what must happen on use? How are Heavy Items/Objects, added Items and Duct Tape handled?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Normal Items hidden in unlimited Inventory, others see backs/colors; used Item shown. Heavy Items/Objects public in two Hands, third requires dropping one. Added Items act as one with base card. Duct Tape combines two Heavy Items into one Hand, never Objects.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Inventory secrecy/back colors/unlimited capacity/reveal-on-use, public two Hands, overflow, attachments and Duct Tape Items-versus-Objects distinction.

question_review.actual_question: What happens to an Item versus an Object voluntarily dropped, when and at what Action cost may you drop, and how do found Weapons differ from starting Weapons in Ammo?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Drop freely during own turn no Action; Objects stay in Room, Items discarded/lost. Found Weapon has 1 Ammo versus starting fully loaded, neither exceeds capacity.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests free own-turn dropping, Room-retained Objects versus discarded Items and searched-one-Ammo versus fully loaded starting Weapons/capacity.

question_review.actual_question: How does Search choose its deck, draw and keep cards, return the rejected card, change the Item Counter, and handle zero Items, Special Rooms and Blue Items?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Search Action: choose one matching Red/Yellow/Green deck, white may choose any ONE, draw two, keep one, put rejected card at BOTTOM of same deck, not shuffle. Lower counter one, zero prevents Search except e.g. Scavenging; Special Rooms cannot Search. Blue Items only Craft.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests deck/color, two draw/one keep/bottom return, counter restriction/exceptions, no Special-Room Search and crafted-only Blue Items.

question_review.actual_question: How does Craft pay its Action and components, must the result be available, can you inspect the deck, and what Crafted Items exist?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Cost one Action card plus discard two Items with blue component icons matching two grey result icons, choose/take available card not random draw; unavailable cannot build. May inspect deck any time. Antidote, Taser, Flamethrower, Molotov Cocktail.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests one-card Craft plus two corresponding component cards, available-result requirement, inspection/selection rather than random draw and four result types.

question_review.actual_question: Who pays for a Trade and who may join; can you give something for nothing, exchange Ammo, or need a separate Pick Up Action for a searched Heavy Item?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Initiator pays one Action card; Characters in same Room may agree to exchange Items/Objects including gifts. Cannot exchange Ammo. Pick Up Heavy Object cost one applies Corpses/Carcasses/Eggs, not searched Heavy Items. All Characters in the Room may trade with each other, including an exchange solely between two Characters who did not pay for the Action.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests initiator payment, all same-Room traders including nonpayers, gifts, no Ammo exchange and no Basic pickup charge for a searched Heavy Item.

question_review.actual_question: How do you reveal Weaknesses: what Object corresponds to each card, where must it be, is it consumed, who benefits and must you personally research for a Discover Weakness Objective?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Character Corpse, Intruder Egg, Intruder Carcass correspond to three face-down slots. Research matching Object present in Laboratory, carried or uncarried, reveal and leave card on board, Object not consumed. Discovered rules benefit all; anyone can do research for Objective.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests three Object/slot matches, Object physically in Laboratory carried or not, not consumed, face-up persistent Weakness and benefits/objective credit regardless researcher.

question_review.actual_question: What are the common prerequisites and cost for Room Actions, what does a Computer icon itself do, and how does Fire affect Room Actions or Searching?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Cost two Action cards, Character in matching Room unless explicit special ability, no Combat or Malfunction. Computer icon only significant when another rule references it, unavailable under Malfunction. Fire alone bars neither Room Action nor Search.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests two-card Room Action and local/functioning/out-of-Combat prerequisites, referenced-only Computer significance and Fire allowing Room Actions/Search.

question_review.actual_question: What exactly does the Armory recharge, by how much, and what limits apply?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Add two Ammo to one Energy Weapon, never Classic Weapons, never above printed capacity.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Armory adding two to one own Energy Weapon only, excluding Classic and respecting capacity.

question_review.actual_question: What are the three mutually exclusive Emergency Room treatments; does dressing remove the Wound or merely its effect, and do identical Serious Wound effects stack?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Dress all Serious OR heal one dressed Serious OR heal all Light. Dress flips/ignores effect but retains Serious count; identical Serious effects do not stack.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests Emergency Room OR menu, dressed effect suppression with retained count and nonstacking identical effects.

question_review.actual_question: What does sending a Signal actually do and what is its game use; can Comms be absent from a normal game?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Comms Room Action puts Status marker on own Signal space, used for Objectives only. Basic Room so always aboard.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests sending Signal as own board marker for Objectives only and guaranteed Comms presence in basic Rooms.

question_review.actual_question: How does Fire Control affect a chosen Room and its Intruders if the Room has Fire, or has none?
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Choose any one Room, remove Fire if present; all its Intruders flee random directions, one Event card drawn per Intruder. Works with no Fire.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests any selected Room Fire removal plus all Intruders fleeing, even absent Fire. Normal retreat Door rules are independently requested at Q68, not overridden here.

question_review.actual_question: Describe starting, stopping and restarting Self-Destruct, advancing it, the yellow threshold, its final space, a jump while active and a Character already hibernating.
question_review.complete_expected_answer: Start marker first green; advance with Time. Stop removes it, restart green. First yellow irreversible/unlocks all Pods, which can relock; subsequent yellow spaces do NOT re-unlock them. Skull or jump with active sequence destroys ship. Characters cannot initiate sequence with anyone hibernating, but Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers.
question_review.independent_scope_and_support_assessment: Requests sequence start/stop/restart/advance/irreversible threshold/final destruction/jump and sleepers. FAQ corrects later-yellow re-unlocking and permits Event initiation despite sleepers.
